maya: FYI after running int8 quant on sea-embed-1 the recall@10 dropped ~6-7% on our wiki holdout. Noticed cosine similarities skew lower. Anyone else see this? :thinking_face:

liam: I saw a small shift in norms on the toy eval yesterday but not that big. What batch/quant pipeline did you use?

maya: used onnxruntime + dynamic quant (per-tensor) from bench ci; config: --quantize=int8 --calibration=5000-samples, batch size 64.

sophia: can you paste the simple recall eval you ran?

maya: sure — quick snippet:```python
# eval snippet
import numpy as np
from sklearn.metrics import pairwise_distances
def recall_at_k(queries, corpus, labels, k=10):
    sims = queries.dot(corpus.T)
    idx = np.argsort(-sims, axis=1)[:, :k]
    return (labels[np.arange(len(queries))[:,None]] == labels[idx]).any(axis=1).mean()
```

liam: rough idea: check l2 norm distribution pre/post quant. Quant can bias low-magnitude dims. Run `np.linalg.norm(embs, axis=1)` hist.

maya: did that — hist shifted left ~10%. Means many vectors shorter.

ben-infra: tagging infra perf — quantized kernels shouldn't change vector direction that much, but rounding can. Did you use per-channel quant or symmetric?

maya: per-tensor symmetric. I can re-run per-channel (onnx supports it) later.

toni: also check whether we applied final L2 normalization in the runtime path. We had a bug last month where normalization was skipped for cached responses.

maya: aha, interesting — I compared the runtime outputs vs offline floats and runtime was missing the normalize call for the quantized model. That explains much.

eval-bot: automated-eval: baseline sea-embed-1 float recall@10=0.812, quant-int8 recall@10=0.745, quant-int8+norm fix recall@10=0.807 (rerun at 1753332301)

sophia: great catch. So two follow-ups: 1) re-run with per-channel quant and normalization enabled, 2) run clustering / silhouette to check semantic structure.

liam: for clustering, run cosine-silhouette on balanced sample (5k per class) and compare. Also compute nearest-neighbor distance ratios: mean(dist_2 / dist_1) to see margin collapse.

maya: planning both. Preliminary per-channel quant + explicit post-process norm brings recall to 0.804 (much closer). Will run the silhouette test and push results.

ben-infra: if per-channel fixes things, update quant pipeline default to per-channel for embed ops, and add a test that validates avg L2 norm within 5% of float baseline.

toni: add a regression alert in optimize: if recall@10 drops >3% after quantization on the gold holdout set, block rollout.

maya: will open a PR with repro script and two artifacts: recall table + norm histograms. Thanks all. :raised_hands:
